cases.description: Classic single-function reentrancy — EtherStore lets an attacker withdraw more than entitled by re-entering before balance is updated.
A view function on contract B (derived from Curve-style pool A) returns stale state during A's mid-execution callback — the read-only reentrancy class.
Proxy.owner lives in slot0; delegatecall to an untrusted Delegate contract lets an attacker overwrite slot0 via the Delegate's own unrelated storage layout, hijacking ownership.
Proxy's implementation-address slot collides with the Logic contract's own state variable (GuestAddress) — classic non-EIP-1967 storage layout collision.
Chainlink ETH/USD feed consumed without a staleness/roundId check — contrasts an unsafe read against a safe one in the same file.
SimpleBank prices collateral off SimplePool's spot reserves — a single-source AMM spot price used as an oracle, manipulable within one transaction.

Classic vault inflation attack: attacker deposits 1 wei then donates directly to inflate the share price, causing the next depositor's shares to round down to a loss — directly matches our own onchain_structural_primitives step2_share_accounting.md research.
transferProxy signature scheme; file's own comments note the nonce starts from 0 ("not a best practice") — a documented near-miss alongside the replay case itself.
Requires a pre-0.8.0 pragma explicitly (file comment: solc >=0.8.0 has built-in overflow checks) — tests the case where the checked-arithmetic default is bypassed by compiler version choice.
EtherGame uses address(this).balance as its win condition; forcing ether in via selfdestruct(attacker-controlled target) desyncs tracked vs actual balance and can brick or grief the game.
